title: Evening Brief — Sat 21 Nov

stories.board: Big AI stock crash shakes Wall Street
stories.headline: US stocks have their worst week in years
stories.what: On Friday the Nasdaq fell about 5.3% and the S&P 500 fell 3.7%. The Dow and S&P 500 are now in a correction (down 10% or more from their top). Nvidia dropped about 14%, and newly listed Anthropic also fell.
stories.why: Many retirement and savings accounts hold these stocks, so a big drop touches lots of families.
stories.sides: No major disagreement on the facts; some outlets call it historic, others say AI stocks were just too expensive.

stories.board: US cyber chief out after tech outages
stories.headline: White House cyber boss replaced after many outages
stories.what: Sean Cairncross, the top White House cyber (computer safety) official, is out after a string of outages hit flights, a big bank, Microsoft 365 and government systems. Pentagon tech chief Kirsten Davies is filling in.
stories.why: When key computer systems fail, planes, banks and offices can stop working.
stories.sides: Fox and some outlets say he was fired; CBS and NBC say he is leaving. Officials say no link to an attack was found, but some experts doubt that.

stories.board: Eisenkot pushes for new Israeli government
stories.headline: Eisenkot calls Likud to nonstop talks on a new government
stories.what: Gadi Eisenkot, who has the job of forming Israel's next government, invited Netanyahu's Likud party to a marathon of talks starting Sunday. Bennett backs a unity (everyone together) government with Eisenkot as prime minister.
stories.why: It decides who will lead Israel next, after Netanyahu lost his majority in the election.
stories.sides: Eisenkot's own camp is split: some want a deal with Likud, others warn against it.

stories.board: Carney signs China deal, holds firm on US
stories.headline: Canada makes a new trade deal with China
stories.what: PM Carney announced a strategic partnership (a closer working deal) with China, which will let in more Canadian food like halibut and shrimp. He says Canada will not rush a trade deal with the US unless it protects car jobs.
stories.why: Trade decides how many Canadian jobs and sales there are, and the US is still our biggest buyer.
stories.sides: The government says it opens new markets; critics say China gets more and could cancel the deal any time.

quick_hits: Israel is getting ready in case Iran strikes first, as reports say the US and Israel weigh new strikes on Iran; Trump has not decided (Ynetnews).
Canada's new budget adds no new money to protect Jewish communities, even as threats and security costs rise (The Hub).
Americans expect prices to rise more slowly: one-year inflation hopes fell to 3.7% in a November survey.
big_picture: A rough week: AI stocks fell hard and computer outages shook the US, while Israel and Canada work on big political and trade choices.
